cases.name: no-filters/everything-matches
cases.note: an unfiltered rule takes the message verbatim as the prompt

cases.name: prefix/stripped-and-trimmed
cases.note: the prompt is what follows the prefix, space-trimmed

cases.name: prefix/case-insensitive
cases.note: EqualFold, so the stored prefix and the sent one may differ in case

cases.name: prefix/ascii-prefix-slices-into-a-multibyte-first-character
cases.note: the sharpest case here. The prefix is one ASCII byte and the message starts with U+212A (three bytes), so text[:1] is a lone continuation byte — invalid UTF-8. Go decodes it as RuneError and does not match. A port slicing by *character* would compare U+212A against 'K' instead; one slicing by byte in Rust would panic.

cases.name: prefix/multibyte-prefix-against-ascii-text
cases.note: the mirror of the case above. A three-byte prefix against ASCII text takes text[:3] — three whole characters — and EqualFold compares three runes against one, so it cannot match however the single rune folds. The fold orbit is exercised by the sigma cases instead, whose forms are all two bytes.

cases.name: prefix/fold-final-sigma
cases.note: EqualFold is simple folding, so final sigma folds to sigma

cases.name: prefix/fold-capital-sigma
cases.note: …and the capital folds to both

cases.name: prefix/dotted-capital-i-does-not-fold-to-ascii-i
cases.note: U+0130 has no simple fold to ASCII 'i'. A port lower-casing instead of folding would disagree, because ToLower(U+0130) begins with one.

cases.name: prefix/no-match
cases.note: a message that does not start with the prefix runs nothing

cases.name: prefix/empty-remainder-is-not-a-match
cases.note: a bare prefix with nothing after it is rejected, not run with an empty prompt

cases.name: prefix/whitespace-only-remainder-is-not-a-match
cases.note: …and neither is one whose remainder trims away

cases.name: prefix/shorter-than-the-prefix-in-bytes
cases.note: the length guard is bytes, and it is what stops the slice below from being out of range

cases.name: prefix/multibyte-text-with-ascii-prefix
cases.note: the byte slice cuts into a multi-byte character: Go compares the broken bytes and does not match, where a char-wise port would either panic or compare something else

cases.name: prefix/multibyte-prefix-matches-itself
cases.note: the same slice is exact when the prefix really is the prefix

cases.name: prefix/nbsp-remainder-trims-away
cases.note: unicode.IsSpace includes U+00A0, so a NBSP-only remainder is empty and the rule does not fire. Rust's char::is_whitespace agrees — both follow White_Space — but that is two standards agreeing, which is why it is pinned rather than assumed.

cases.name: prefix/nel-remainder-trims-away
cases.note: U+0085 is unicode.IsSpace, so this remainder is empty

cases.name: keywords/or-logic
cases.note: any keyword matching is enough

cases.name: keywords/case-insensitive-both-sides
cases.note: the text and the keyword are both lower-cased

cases.name: keywords/substring-not-word
cases.note: Contains, so a keyword inside a longer word matches

cases.name: chat-ids/exact-string-compare
cases.note: the id is compared as text, so a leading zero is a different chat

cases.name: chat-ids/negative-group-id
cases.note: group chats have negative ids and are compared the same way

cases.name: all-three/prefix-strips-before-keywords-are-checked-against-the-FULL-text
cases.note: the keyword check runs against `text`, not the stripped prompt — so a keyword that appears only inside the prefix still matches

cases.name: all-three/keyword-only-in-prefix
cases.note: the sharp edge of the clause above: the prompt has no 'deploy' in it at all, and the rule still fires
